gbm_population_evidence.quote: Low Grade Glioma (LGG) of Brain With BRAF Aberration; High Grade Glioma (HGG) of the Brain With BRAF Aberration; Low Grade Glioma of Brain With Neurofibromatosis Type 1
Stratum 4 HGG with BRAF V600E/D/K mutation

candidate_evidence.quote: Giving hydroxychloroquine with trametinib and/or dabrafenib may lower the chance of brain tumors growing or spreading compared to usual treatments.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Recurrent LGG or HGG With a BRAF Aberration

role_evidence.quote: Hydroxychloroquine, works in different ways to stop the growth of tumor cells by killing the cells or stopping them from dividing.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: autophagy inhibition to address resistance to RAF and MEK inhibitors

role_evidence.quote: adding hydroxychloroquine to dabrafenib and/or trametinib
adding hydroxychloroquine to dabrafenib and/or trametinib

source_quote.quote: BRAF alterations will be locally determined using molecular methods in a Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act (CLIA)-certified laboratory.

flag.reason: BRAF alteration is an entry requirement and matches the dabrafenib/trametinib backbone, but the candidate (hydroxychloroquine, an autophagy inhibitor) has no direct BRAF link; coded not matched.

coder_notes: Population is BRAF-altered low- and high-grade glioma in children and young adults; glioblastoma is never named, so high_grade_glioma_unspecified. Dabrafenib and trametinib are the backbone to which hydroxychloroquine is added (manual C3 example). MAPK aberrations by exome sequencing and LC3II/p62 are exploratory or pharmacodynamic and not listed separately.
